title: Finite type algebraic-space fibre dimension as a supremum of local relative dimensions
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $t\in T$ put $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For $x\in|X|$, put $t=f(x)$. A chart at $x$ means a representable etale map $U\to X$ from an affine scheme and a point $u\in U$ mapping to $x$. Write $U_t=U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $\widetilde u\in U_t$ for the unique point mapping to $u$. Write $\dim_{\widetilde u}U_t$ for the minimum of the Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods of $\widetilde u$ in $U_t$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Define $\delta_f(x)=\sup_{(U,u)}\dim_{\widetilde u}U_t$ over these charts. Assume in addition that $f$ is quasi-compact, meaning that its pullback to every quasi-compact scheme has a quasi-compact scheme atlas, so $f$ is of finite type. Define $n_f(t)$ to be the supremum of the topological Krull dimensions of all affine schemes with a representable etale map to $X_t$, with empty supremum $-\infty$. Then
$$n_f(t)=\sup_{x\in|X|,\ f(x)=t}\delta_f(x)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots\}.$$
The fibre is empty exactly when there is no $x\in|X|$ with $f(x)=t$, in which case both suprema are $-\infty$. If the fibre is nonempty, its dimension is the largest integer $\delta_f(x)$ among points over $t$. No separatedness, properness, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$ and an affine open $V\subset T$ containing it. Put $X_V=X\times_TV$. The quasi-compactness hypothesis gives a quasi-compact scheme atlas of $X_V$; [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement] replaces it by a surjective etale atlas $a:U\to X_V$ with $U$ affine. The composite $U\to X$ is etale: on each scheme test it is the composite of the etale atlas projection and the open immersion induced by $V\subset T$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The compatible-chart meaning of local finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives that $U\to V$ is locally of finite type. Set $P=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and locally of finite type over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Its affine source is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so its structure morphism to the spectrum of a field is quasi-compact: that target has only the opens empty and itself. Hence $P$ is finite type over the field by the definition. Base change gives a surjective etale atlas $P\to X_t$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 0D4M (lemma-dimension-fibre), proof, last paragraph with scheme target and residue-field fibre; chart invariance uses descent.tex Tag 04N4.

proof.text: For a point $x\in|X|$ over $t$, choose $u\in U$ over $x$. Such $u$ exists because the atlas surjects onto $X_V$ and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives a point of $X_V$ above the compatible pair $(x,t)$. The scheme-fibre homeomorphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre] gives a unique $p\in P$ above $u$. Consider any other affine etale chart $b:W\to X$ and $w\in W$ over $x$. The scheme $R=U\times_XW$ has etale projections, and [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $r\in R$ over $(u,w)$. The unique point of the scheme fibre $R_t$ over $r$ maps to $p$ and to the point $\widetilde w\in W_t$. Its projections to $P$ and $W_t$ are etale by the scheme-test definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point] to both projections: $\dim_pP=\dim_{\widetilde w}W_t$. Thus every term defining $\delta_f(x)$ has the value $\dim_pP$, and at least one term occurs, namely $(U,u)$. Therefore $\delta_f(x)=\dim_pP$, independently of every choice.

source.place: Tag 0D4M (lemma-dimension-fibre), proof, last paragraph with scheme target and residue-field fibre; chart invariance uses descent.tex Tag 04N4.

proof.text: For any affine etale chart $B\to X_t$ and any $b\in B$, lift $b$ to a point $r$ of $B\times_{X_t}P$, using surjectivity of the base-changed atlas [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Write $p$ for its image in $P$. Both projections are etale, so [lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point] gives $\dim_bB=\dim_pP\leq\dim P$. The supremum formula [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] now gives $\dim B\leq\dim P$. Since $P$ itself is an affine etale chart of $X_t$, taking the supremum over $B$ yields $n_f(t)=\dim P$. This compares chart dimension only; no identification with $\dim|X_t|$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0D4M (lemma-dimension-fibre), proof, last paragraph with scheme target and residue-field fibre; chart invariance uses descent.tex Tag 04N4.

proof.text: Every $p\in P$ maps to a point $x\in|X|$ over $t$, and step 2 gives $\dim_pP=\delta_f(x)$. Conversely every such $x$ has a lift $p$ as constructed in step 2. Hence the two families have the same set of values. Taking suprema and using [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\sup_{f(x)=t}\delta_f(x)=\sup_{p\in P}\dim_pP=\dim P=n_f(t)$.

source.place: Tag 0D4M (lemma-dimension-fibre), proof, last paragraph with scheme target and residue-field fibre; chart invariance uses descent.tex Tag 04N4.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], the finite type scheme $P$ over $\kappa(t)$ has finite dimension. If $P$ is nonempty its local dimensions are nonnegative integers bounded by this finite dimension. Their nonempty set has a largest element, and its supremum is that element. Steps 2 and 4 transfer attainment to a point $x$ over $t$. Finally the atlas and step 2 show that $P$ is nonempty exactly when a point $x$ over $t$ exists, and that this is equivalent to $X_t$ being nonempty. If $X_t$ is empty, any scheme mapping to it is empty; all chart dimensions and both displayed suprema are $-\infty$. This proves the empty clause and excludes $+\infty$ without any extra separation or flatness hypothesis.

It splits the unchanged item into 5 steps and adds no new nodes. The steps follow the last paragraph of Stacks 0D4M (spaces-more-morphisms l.7168-7180). Step 1: the qc atlas refinement (03H6) gives an affine atlas U of X_V; P = U x_V Spec kappa(t) is affine and of finite type over the field, and P -> X_t is a surjective etale atlas. Step 2: chart independence is proved inline through R = U x_X W; R_t -> P and R_t -> W_t are etale by the scheme-test definition, and 04N4 (descent l.5173, cited through the existing Q11 node lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point) gives the equal local dimensions. Step 3: any affine chart B of X_t has dim B <= dim P (04N4 plus 0B7I), so n_f(t) = dim P. Steps 4 and 5 are elementary: reindexing, and finiteness from lem-kun-dimension-finite-type. Every cited statement supports its use. No separatedness is used. Small cases tested: A^1 with an extra point, empty fibre, t outside the image, imperfect residue field, non-separated X. The sibling lem-sfb-space-local-fibre-dimension-open also states chart independence; the item reproves it inline, which is redundant but correct and creates no duplicate node. Batch-5 flags: lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus (Stacks 03H4/03H5/03BX point calculus; its closure reaches only the definition def-trf-algebraic-space) and lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement (Stacks 03H6/03E4) are general algebraic-space foundations. lean.statement: theorem fibre_dimension_eq_supremum {T : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace T) (hft : ∀ (U : Over T) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (hqc : ∀ (V : Over T), CompactSpace V.left → ∃ (U : Over T) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Limits.prod X.obj.obj (yoneda.obj V)), CompactSpace U.left ∧ IsEtale a ∧ IsSurjective a) (t : T) : ((⨆ (U : Over T) (_ : IsAffine U.left) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ residueFibrePresheaf X t) (_ : IsEtale a), topologicalKrullDim U.left) = ⨆ (x : Point X.obj.obj) (_ : pointLiesOver X t x), localFibreDimension X x) ∧ (IsEmpty (Point (residueFibrePresheaf X t)) ↔ ¬ ∃ x : Point X.obj.obj, pointLiesOver X t x) ∧ (IsEmpty (Point (residueFibrePresheaf X t)) → (⨆ (U : Over T) (_ : IsAffine U.left) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ residueFibrePresheaf X t) (_ : IsEtale a), topologicalKrullDim U.left) = ⊥ ∧ (⨆ (x : Point X.obj.obj) (_ : pointLiesOver X t x), localFibreDimension X x) = ⊥) ∧ (Nonempty (Point (residueFibrePresheaf X t)) → ∃ (d : ℕ) (x : Point X.obj.obj), pointLiesOver X t x ∧ localFibreDimension X x = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ (⨆ (U : Over T) (_ : IsAffine U.left) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ residueFibrePresheaf X t) (_ : IsEtale a), topologicalKrullDim U.left) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
lean.note: The structural morphism is encoded by X : AlgebraicSpace T. The canonical residue-field fibre is the presheaf product over the terminal h_T. The theorem spells out the affine-chart supremum rather than using the topological dimension of Point. Reuses the real-data localFibreDimension definition through def-sfb-space-local-fibre-dimension, which binds its existing landed declaration. The separate chart-independence/openness theorem is not a statement dependency. pointLiesOver expresses the base image through field-valued representatives without choosing one.
